subject: a vintage brass and painted metal double helix DNA molecular model on a stand, the kind built in a 1950s laboratory
style: science museum artifact, aged brass and enamel
caption: The Watson and Crick model. Genes set a range of possibilities; environment decides where inside that range you land.

subject: a single motor neuron, cell body with branching dendrites and one long myelinated axon ending in terminal buttons
style: anatomical specimen, soft pink and pale violet tissue
caption: One neuron. Everything the nervous system does is billions of these passing a signal in one direction only.

hotspots.title: Dendrites
hotspots.note: Receive signals from other neurons. More branches means more incoming connections.

hotspots.title: Cell body
hotspots.note: Sums the incoming signals. Cross the threshold and the neuron fires, all or nothing.

hotspots.title: Myelin sheath
hotspots.note: Fatty insulation. It speeds the impulse up; when it breaks down you get multiple sclerosis.

hotspots.title: Terminal buttons
hotspots.note: Release neurotransmitters into the synapse. The signal goes chemical here.

subject: a laboratory oscilloscope with a green trace showing a single sharp action potential spike on its round screen
style: mid century scientific instrument, grey enamel and brass dials
caption: The action potential as Adrian recorded it. All or nothing: the spike is always the same size, only the rate changes.

subject: a human brain, three quarter lateral view, cerebellum and brainstem visible
caption: The lobes, the cerebellum, and the brainstem. Damage in one place changes one kind of behaviour, which is how we mapped it.

hotspots.title: Frontal lobe
hotspots.note: Planning, judgment, personality, and speech production (Broca). The Phineas Gage lobe.

hotspots.title: Parietal lobe
hotspots.note: Touch, temperature, pain, and body position. Home of the somatosensory cortex.

hotspots.title: Occipital lobe
hotspots.note: Vision. Damage here can blind you even with perfectly healthy eyes.

hotspots.title: Temporal lobe
hotspots.note: Hearing and language comprehension (Wernicke). Wraps around the hippocampus.

hotspots.title: Cerebellum
hotspots.note: Balance, coordination, and procedural (muscle memory) learning.

hotspots.title: Brainstem
hotspots.note: Breathing, heartbeat, and arousal. The parts you never have to think about.

subject: an EEG electrode cap, a mesh skull cap covered in small round silver electrodes with coloured wires gathered behind
caption: How we know sleep has stages. Aserinsky and Kleitman watched these traces and found REM in 1953.

subject: a human eyeball anatomical model, sectioned to show the lens, the iris and the retina at the back, with the optic nerve attached
caption: Sensation is transduction: light becomes a neural signal at the retina. Everything after that is the brain guessing well.

hotspots.title: Lens
hotspots.note: Changes shape to focus light on the retina. Accommodation is this muscle at work.

hotspots.title: Retina
hotspots.note: Rods for dim light and motion, cones for colour and detail. Transduction happens here.

hotspots.title: Optic nerve
hotspots.note: Carries the signal out. Where it leaves there are no receptors, which is your blind spot.
